_why_two_claims: AGREEMENT asks whether the engines compute the same thing; RECOVERY asks whether they compute the right thing. Neither implies the other.

truth.source: the fixture's data-generating process: ATT = 2 + 2.0 E[severity | treated], integrated by fixture.truth_att() and checked with scipy quad

agreement.claim: both engines build the same matched set and report the same ATT, pair-clustered SE and balance
agreement._note: Observed spread on the committed fixture: 0 in every key; the Python greedy matcher reproduces MatchIt's 733 pairs exactly. Local R had MatchIt 4.8.0; CI installs 4.7.2 from the snapshot. harness/causal_examples.test.py replays the greedy order by brute force, checks the caliper and that no control is reused, and requires balance under 0.1 after matching (0.06) from over 0.3 before (0.50).

recovery.claim: the ATT is close to the fixture's

calibration.rule: about 1.3 times the measured 99th percentile miss, rounded up
calibration.limits: The ATT and ATE differ by 0.68; the tolerance keeps them apart. A first fixture (900 patients, a stronger propensity model) dropped 46 treated at the caliper on average and its miss (0.53) could not tell the ATT from the ATE. Measured by harness/causal_examples.test.py, running python.py on seeds 0 to 99.
